title: termal_evaluate_acceptance refuses with 'no sighting of named source root' although the root was named before edits and later checkpoints were taken (Kimi session, Engram project, 2026-10-29)
outcome: A session that names its source root before editing and then checkpoints has a named-root sighting at the evidence basis, so termal_evaluate_acceptance can run. Where a runtime cannot produce sightings, the host says so in a typed, actionable way at naming time, not only at evaluation time.
acceptance: A cause note identifies why no sighting existed for generation 2219 at cuts 17 and 21 (runtime support, capture path, or checkpoint semantics), with file:line and evidence.

When a session names its source root during a turn, the naming response states that the root takes effect at the session's next turn and that acceptance evaluation needs a later turn that opens in the named root. An acceptance evaluation requested before any turn has opened in the newly named root is refused before the Engram read, with a typed, actionable reason saying so. The refusal for an absent sighting names, as its remedy, a turn that opens in the named root after the naming. Deterministic tests cover: name mid-turn, then evaluate, gives the typed refusal; and after the next gated turn opens in the named root, the evaluation preflight proceeds past the sighting check.

When turn-gated control is off for the naming session's project, successful root naming includes a typed, actionable notice that another ordinary turn does not produce a mediated named-root sighting. If the normal sighting read returns absent, acceptance refuses with the same actionable limitation rather than prescribing a focus-only checkpoint as a guaranteed remedy. An existing matching sighting still permits preflight under OFF. Deterministic tests cover OFF naming, OFF absent-sighting refusal, OFF present-sighting success, and retain the gated naming-turn and later-opening controls. No automatic gating change, fabricated observation, sighting waiver or shell-touch requirement is introduced.
